The GP terms are \(4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192\). A common term must be \(\equiv 1 \pmod 5\):

The bracket is the Riemann sum \(\sum_{k=1}^{n} f(k/n)\):
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{2}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n} f\!\left(\frac{k}{n}\right)=2\int_0^1 \log_2\!\left(1+\tan\tfrac{\pi x}{4}\right)dx = 2I.\]
Apply \(x\to 1-x\): \(\tan\frac{\pi(1-x)}{4}=\frac{1-t}{1+t}\) with \(t=\tan\frac{\pi x}{4}\), so
\[1+\tan\tfrac{\pi(1-x)}{4}=\frac{2}{1+t}\Rightarrow \log_2(\cdots)=1-\log_2(1+t).\]
Adding the two forms of \(I\): \(2I=\int_0^1 1\,dx=1\Rightarrow I=\tfrac12\).
\[2I = 1.\]

Place \(A=(0,0),B=(1,0),C=(1,1),D=(0,1)\). \(C_2\) is tangent to \(AB,AD\), so its centre is \((r,r)\) with radius \(r\). Internal tangency with \(C_1\) (centre \(A\), radius \(1\)):
\[r\sqrt2 = 1-r \Rightarrow r=\frac{1}{\sqrt2+1}=\sqrt2-1.\]
Let \(E=(e,0)\). Line \(CE\) through \((1,1),(e,0)\) is \(x-(1-e)y-e=0\); tangency to \(C_2\) gives
\[\frac{e(1-r)}{\sqrt{1+(1-e)^2}}=r.\]
With \(1-r=2-\sqrt2\) and \(r=\sqrt2-1\), squaring yields \(2e^2=2-2e+e^2\Rightarrow e^2+2e-2=0\Rightarrow e=\sqrt3-1\).
\[EB=1-e=2-\sqrt3=\alpha+\sqrt3\,\beta\Rightarrow \alpha=2,\ \beta=-1,\ \alpha+\beta=1.\]

Expand about \(x=0\): \(ae^x-b\cos x+ce^{-x}\)
\[=(a-b+c)+(a-c)x+\frac{a+b+c}{2}x^2+\cdots,\qquad x\sin x\sim x^2.\]
For a finite limit the constant and linear terms must vanish:
\[a-b+c=0,\qquad a-c=0.\]
Then
\[\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tfrac{a+b+c}{2}x^2}{x^2}=\frac{a+b+c}{2}=2\Rightarrow a+b+c=4.\]

\(\operatorname{tr}(AA^T)=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^2\), so we count 9-tuples of entries from \(\{0,1,2,3\}\) with squares summing to \(9\). Available squares: \(0,1,4,9\).
\[9=9:\ \text{one entry }3\Rightarrow \binom{9}{1}=9.\]
\[9=4+4+1:\ \text{two }2\text{'s, one }1\Rightarrow \binom{9}{2}\binom{7}{1}=36\cdot7=252.\]
\[9=4+1{\cdot}5:\ \text{one }2,\ \text{five }1\text{'s}\Rightarrow \binom{9}{1}\binom{8}{5}=9\cdot56=504.\]
\[9=1{\cdot}9:\ \text{nine }1\text{'s}\Rightarrow 1.\]
\[9+252+504+1=766.\]

Since \(P^{-1}AP-I_3=P^{-1}(A-I_3)P\), similarity preserves the determinant:
\[\det\big((P^{-1}AP-I_3)^2\big)=\big(\det(A-I_3)\big)^2.\]
Here \(A-I_3=\begin{bmatrix}1&7&\omega^2\\-1&-(\omega+1)&1\\0&-\omega&-\omega\end{bmatrix}\). Expanding:
\[\det(A-I_3)=\big(\omega(\omega+1)+\omega\big)-7\omega+\omega^2\cdot\omega=\omega^2-5\omega+\omega^3.\]
Using \(\omega^3=1\) and \(\omega^2=-1-\omega\): \(=(-1-\omega)-5\omega+1=-6\omega\).
\[\big(\det(A-I_3)\big)^2=36\omega^2=\alpha\omega^2\Rightarrow \alpha=36.\]

\[\text{Area}=\left|\int_{-m}^{m}(u^2+k)\,du\right|=\frac{4}{3}(-k)^{3/2}.\]
Set equal to \(\dfrac{4\sqrt8}{3}\): \((-k)^{3/2}=\sqrt8\Rightarrow -k=8^{1/3}=2\Rightarrow k=-2\).

\[y(1)=1+2-1=2.\]

\[\int_a^{a+2}f=\int_a^{a+1}f+\int_{a+1}^{a+2}f=\int_a^{a+1}f(x)\,dx+\int_a^{a+1}\big(2-f(x)\big)\,dx=2,\]
so every interval of length \(2\) integrates to \(2\). Hence
\[I_1=\int_0^8 f=4\cdot2=8,\qquad I_2=\int_{-1}^{3} f=2\cdot2=4.\]

\(\left|\frac{z+i}{z-3i}\right|=1\) means \(z\) is equidistant from \(-i\) and \(3i\), i.e. the perpendicular bisector \(y=1\); write \(z=x+i\). Then \(z\bar z=|z|^2=x^2+1\) and
\[w=(x^2+1)-2(x+i)+2=(x^2-2x+3)-2i.\]
\(\operatorname{Re}(w)=x^2-2x+3\) is minimised at \(x=1\), giving \(w=2-2i\), with \(\arg w=-\tfrac{\pi}{4}\).
\[w^n\ \text{real}\iff n\cdot\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=k\pi\iff n=4k,\]
so the minimum \(n=4\).
